messages.author: af386179fe1eb913
messages.subject: cluster argument error
parts:
Hi everyone,

I wonder if anyone can shed any light on the error that I get when I try use the cluster argument (for a configural invariance model, shown below, though the same error arises for multiple models).

Error in lav_data_cluster_patterns(Y = X[[g]], clus = clus, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan ERROR: everything cluster contains only one observation.

The model (and others) ran without any errors when I ran previously, and now I am trying to rerun with no luck!

I am new to the group so I'm not sure what information is needed, but here is my syntax:

model_22 <-
  'p22 =~ p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5 + p6 + p7 + p8 + p9 + p10 + p11 + p12 + p13 + p14 + p15'
fit_model_22 <- cfa(model_22, data=data, group = "random", cluster = "famID", estimator = "MLR", std.lv=F, missing = "fiml")
summary(fit_model_22, fit.measures=T, standardized=T)

N = 13555, with two family members per family (so two rows / participants have the same value for "famID").

Any help would be hugely appreciated.

Many thanks,
Laura

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: cluster argument error
parts:
On 2/14/22 16:26, Laura Havers wrote:
> Error in lav_data_cluster_patterns(Y = X[[g]], clus = clus, cluster =
> cluster,  :
>   lavaan ERROR: everything cluster contains only one observation.

The error message (where 'everything' should be 'every', will fix that)
indicates that each cluster has only 1 observation.

> model_22 <-
>   'p22 =~ p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5 + p6 + p7 + p8 + p9 + p10 + p11 + p12
> + p13 + p14 + p15'
> fit_model_22 <- cfa(model_22, data=data, group = "random", cluster =
> "famID", estimator = "MLR", std.lv=F, missing = "fiml")
> summary(fit_model_22, fit.measures=T, standardized=T)

> N = 13555, with two family members per family (so two rows /
> participants have the same value for "famID").

What is the "random" variable? I think you need to remove the group =
"random" altogether.

As you seem to have two family members only, you may consider reshaping
your data in 'wide format', so that the variables of the two family
members are in the same row, and the rows become the families.

See: https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2019.1689366

This paper is mostly about categorical data, but it works equally well
with continuous data.

Yves.

parts:
Just to close the loop on this thread.. I'm just posting this response below from Yves (with my questions interspersed) in case it's useful for others / in the future

>
>         On 2/22/22 12:44, Laura Havers wrote:
>          > Just to check my understanding in that case, does this mean
>         that the
>          > standard errors (and test statistic, I believe) are only
>         adjusted where
>          > there is clustering *within groups (and that there is no need
>         for
>          > correction where there is clustering *across groups)?
>
>         Hm. If you have both groups and clusters, then the groups must
>         be on the
>         highest level. For example, students in (a random sample of)
>         schools, in
>         two countries. Here, countries would be the group variable, and
>         school
>         the cluster variable.
>
>         As soon as the cluster sizes are larger than 1, we need to
>         'correct' for
>         the clustering.
>
>         It is in general not possible to have groups within clusters. An
>         example
>         would be male and female students in schools. We could have
>         'gender' as
>         a covariate in a multilevel SEM, but we can not treat 'gender' as a
>         'group' in a multigroup analysis. The reason is that the latter
>         requires
>         that the groups are independent.
>
>          > I'm puzzled though... I previously ran some measurement
>         invariance
>          > models using the same specification (i.e., group = random,
>         cluster =
>          > family), and the models ran without error (I know this
>         because I have
>          > the results!). Am I going completely mad, or might there have
>         been an
>          > update or something similar to lavaan over the past year or
>         so that
>          > could have previously allowed the models to run?
>
>         That could be. I do not remember when this 'check' has been
>         introduced,
>         but it is very likely that it was not there (yet) in the early
>         releases
>         of the 0.6 series.
>
>         In any case, the (older) results should be very similar to what
>         you get
>         if you omit the cluster= argument altogether. Assuming there is
>         only a
>         single observation in each cluster.
>
>         Yves.
>
>         --
